accuracy.evidence: Checked against NASA Science and the IAU: most known asteroids orbit in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter and most are irregular in shape; Ceres is about 940 km across, the largest object in the belt and a dwarf planet; comets are ice, dust and rock whose ice sublimates near the Sun into a coma and tails that point away from the Sun (radiation pressure and solar wind), so the tail leads an outbound comet; meteoroid in space, meteor in the atmosphere, meteorite on the ground, and most meteoroids burn up; IAU Resolution B5 (24 August 2006) defines a planet by three tests and a dwarf planet by the first two; Pluto's orbital period is about 248 years; Halley's Comet returns about every 76 years (1986, next 2061). The strip of planets is labelled as a row, not a scale map.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented children's ideas from NASA Space Place and primary astronomy misconception lists: the tail trails behind like smoke (step 2 predict, 'going' ring, p2, challenge tag behind), comets are burning (Ava, m1), a shooting star is a falling star (step 3 predict, Gus, m3), meteor and meteorite are the same word (lab drops with six pair-specific messages, p4, challenge tag meteor), asteroids sit near Earth or are round (belt drops, m7), Pluto was demoted because it shrank or stopped orbiting (step 4 predict, Ela, Flo, m5), and the Moon could be a dwarf planet (sort, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). Related lessons 574 naming the planets and the solar system lesson order planets; 966 telescopes is about light. This lab is about small bodies only: a planet strip where asteroids are dropped by zone (inner, belt, gas giants, Kuiper Belt each answer differently), a comet dragged round an ellipse with the Sun at a focus whose tail length follows distance and whose direction follows the Sun-comet line, name tags dropped on a rock in space, in the air and on the ground, and a three-rule planet test panel.

lab_teaches.evidence: The tail is computed from position, so children see it vanish far out, grow near the Sun and point ahead of the comet at the 'going' ring before the text names the rule. Wrong asteroid drops explain what is there instead (few near Earth, icy Kuiper Belt). Tapping a body lights its three rule checks, so Pluto and Ceres visibly fail only 'Cleared its path' and the Moon fails 'Goes round the Sun'. Rock sizes shrink from space to ground, showing that most burns up.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks where most asteroids are with 'Between Earth and the Moon' tempting; the belt drop disproves it. Step 2 asks which way the tail points with 'Behind it, the way it came' tempting; the 'going' ring shows the tail in front. Step 3 asks what a shooting star is with 'A star falling to Earth' tempting. Step 4 asks why Pluto changed with 'It got smaller' tempting; the rule panel shows it fails only the cleared-path test.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every distractor has its own tag and message: moon and kuiper (belt location), behind and towards (tail pushed away from the Sun), meteor and meteoroid (which stage lands), mars and moon2 (planet vs moon), always and far (tail only near the Sun), round and gas (asteroids are lumpy solid rock). Lab feedback names the slip, for example 'Only a rock that lands is a meteorite. This one is still out in space.' and 'Not dwarf planet. Earth goes round the Sun, is round and has cleared its path.'

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 1.9 (limit 6.5) and the adult text 5.6 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Far from the Sun it is frozen.'); precise terms (asteroid belt, nucleus, coma, meteoroid, meteor, meteorite, dwarf planet, orbit, Kuiper Belt, cleared its orbit) are in the key idea and adult text.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph matches one lab step (belt, comet tail, the three meteor words, the planet tests); the adult text gives curriculum links, the five tasks and the named mistakes; hints point back to a specific ring, rock or rule in the lab.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android) for every step at start, mid Show me and end, plus desktop. After the first pass the planet labels were placed by a collision check (rows above and below) so Mercury, Earth and Mars no longer run together and Jupiter clears the belt box, the Kuiper Belt label moved to the top right, the orbit was narrowed so the 'far' ring and the perihelion tail stay inside the panel, and the meteor name boxes were moved so they no longer overlap each other or the 'air' label. Every drag target is at least 40 px and every action also has a full-width button.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completes with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Put an asteroid near Earth / between Mars and Jupiter / past Neptune, Move the comet on / back, Call the space rock a …, Put <body> in Planet / Dwarf planet / Neither, '<name> is right'), and the aria-label is rewritten after each action with how many asteroids are in the belt, how near the Sun the comet is and whether it has a tail, which rocks are named, and the selected body's three rule results.
